source: Keller A, Vosshall LB. Olfactory perception of chemically diverse molecules. BMC Neurosci 2016;17:55. doi:10.1186/s12868-016-0287-2. Data: CC0 (Additional file 1).

steps.reason: demographics, DREAM subject number and free-text descriptions are not used (PLAN 4.4)

steps.coding: random permutation (seed 2026) -> P01..P55; key kept private

molecules.name: isobutyl acetate
molecules.method: PubChem lookup of the name (CAS not found)

steps.rule: CID, name and CAS compared on the structure skeleton (InChIKey connectivity block); two sources against one decide, otherwise the sheet CID is kept and flagged
dilution in paraffin oil; log10 of the dilution fraction; within each molecule the stronger one = high

steps.conversion: none needed: every scale is a 0-100 slider

flag_rules.low_retest_intensity: test-retest r of intensity < 0.2 (agreed rule for the sensitivity analysis)
flag_rules.few_retest_pairs: fewer than 10 repeated stimuli detected both times (r unreliable)
flag_rules.narrow_scale: SD of pleasantness < 10 (uses a narrow part of the scale)
flag_rules.extreme_mean: mean pleasantness or intensity more than 2 SD from the panel
flag_rules.high_nondetect: does not detect more than 50% of stimuli

steps.action: flagged only, nothing removed; z-scoring per subject is applied in the analyses, raw values kept

steps.rule: mapped only if the meaning is the same AND rho >= 0.3; analyses use the 20 Keller descriptors directly, the mapping is only for comparison with the odor model
steps.evidence: Spearman rho across molecules: panel-mean descriptor rating (detected, 1st presentation, both concentrations pooled) vs odor-model probability
